title: How are grammatical and arithmetic processing related in the brain? An ALE meta-analysis
title_zh: 语法与算术处理在大脑中的关联：ALE荟萃分析
abstract: Grammatical and arithmetic skills are consistently associated, but the nature of this relationship remains debated. On the one hand, it may be due to shared linguistic processes. On the other hand, it may also come from domain-general abilities involved in extracting and applying abstract structured rules. To address this question, we investigated the neural basis of the relation between grammatical and arithmetic processing by conducting an activation likelihood estimation (ALE) meta-analysis of whole-brain fMRI studies of grammatical (n = 50 experiments) and arithmetic (n = 70 experiments) processing in healthy children and adults. Left perisylvian language regions were more consistently recruited for grammatical than arithmetic processing, whereas bilateral parietal regions were more consistently recruited for arithmetic than grammatical processing. The conjunction analysis revealed overlapping activation in four left-lateralized regions: the junction between the Inferior and Middle Frontal Gyrus, the Supplementary Motor Area, the Parietal Lobule, and the Anterior Insula. Together, these findings indicate that grammatical and arithmetic processing recruit both shared and domain-specific neural systems. The overlapping regions largely correspond to areas associated with the multiple-demand network, suggesting that both domains engage domain-general cognitive mechanisms involved in complex rule-based processing. In contrast, classical perisylvian language regions were selectively recruited during grammatical processing, whereas bilateral parietal regions were more consistently associated with arithmetic processing. These findings therefore suggest that the relation between grammar and arithmetic is better explained by the coexistence of shared domain-general mechanisms and domain-specific neural systems than by shared linguistic processes alone.
abstract_zh: 语法与算术技能始终相关，但其关系的本质仍有争议。一方面，可能是由于共享的语言过程；另一方面，也可能源于涉及提取和应用抽象结构规则的领域通用能力。为了解答此问题，我们通过对健康儿童和成人的语法（n = 50 试验）与算术（n = 70 试验）fMRI 全脑研究进行激活可能性估计（ALE）荟萃分析，探讨了语法与算术处理关系的神经基础。结果显示，左侧围颞语言区在语法处理时比算术处理更一致地被招募，而双侧顶叶区在算术处理时比语法处理更一致地被招募。并置分析揭示了四个左侧化区域的重叠激活：下额叶与中额叶交界处、补充运动区、顶叶小叶和前岛。综合来看，这些发现表明语法与算术处理既招募共享的也招募领域特异的神经系统。重叠区域大多对应多需求网络（multiple-demand network）相关区域，提示两领域都涉及用于复杂规则处理的领域通用认知机制。相反，经典的围颞语言区在语法处理时被选择性招募，而双侧顶叶区在算术处理时更一致地与之相关。因此，这些结果表明，语法与算术之间的关系更能通过共享的领域通用机制与领域特异神经系统的共存来解释，而非仅仅通过共享的语言过程。
